title: #003. Carry-On Packing & Integers

# #003. Carry-On Packing & Integers

<!-- section:scenario -->
Pack integer quantities `counts[i]` of $n$ item types into a bag with weight limit `maxWeight`, maximizing total value while respecting `0 <= counts[i] <= maxCounts[i]`.

Right now the starter code has **two intentional gaps**:
1. It omits the weight limit constraint (`sum(weight[i] * counts[i]) <= maxWeight`), so running it immediately triggers a **VIOLATION**.
2. The items must be packed in **integer** units (`counts[i]` cannot be fractional!). Switch the variable constructor from continuous to integer (`m.integer` in WaSHI, `h.addIntegral` in `highspy`).

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input**: `maxWeight: number`, `weights: number[]`, `values: number[]`, `maxCounts: number[]`
- **Output**: `{ counts: number[], totalValue: number }` (where every `counts[i]` is an integer)

<!-- section:example -->
With `maxWeight = 10`, `weights = [3, 4, 2]`, `values = [40, 55, 22]`, `maxCounts = [2, 2, 3]`, packing `counts = [2, 1, 0]` weighs $2\times 3 + 1\times 4 = 10$ for maximum integer value **`135`**.

<!-- section:hint1 -->
- **WaSHI**: Declare integer arrays with `m.integer("item_" + i, { lb: 0, ub: cap })` inside `map`, and add the weight limit using `` expr`dot(${input.weights}, ${counts}) <= ${input.maxWeight}` ``.
- **highspy**: Use `h.addIntegral(lb=0, ub=cap, name=f"item_{i}")` and add `h.addConstr(h.qsum(w * x for w, x in zip(weights, counts)) <= input_data["maxWeight"])`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Without the integer requirement (`continuous`), packing fractional units can reach higher LP relaxation values that are physically impossible for whole items! Using `Math.round(...)` (`round(...)` in Python) when reading solved integer variables also safely cleans `1.999999999` tolerances.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v_i x_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} w_i x_i \le W_{\max} \\
& x_i \in \{0, 1, \dots, u_i\} \quad \forall i
\end{aligned}
$$
